messages.content: Write the engineering culture section of a careers page. Around 250 words.

output:
**Engineering Culture**

We hire people who like finishing things. Most of our engineers own a feature end to end — from the first design doc through the on-call rotation after it ships. If something breaks at 2am, the person who built it is the person we call, and we think that's the right trade for the ownership it buys.

We keep the review bar high but the cycle short. A pull request gets a real read within a few hours, not a rubber stamp and not a week of silence. We'd rather argue about a design in a comment thread than discover the disagreement in production.

We write things down. Decisions live in docs, not in one person's head, because the team is small enough that any of us might be out sick the week a question comes up. New hires read the same design docs the founders wrote on day one.

We don't do hero culture. Late nights happen, but if they happen every sprint, that's a planning problem, not a personality trait we're selecting for. We'd rather ship something smaller and correct than something large and shaky.

Most of the codebase is legible enough that you can read a file cold and understand why it looks the way it does — no tribal knowledge required to make a change safely. We invest time in tests and tooling because paying that cost once beats paying it every week.

If you want a job where you write code and then watch someone else own it forever, this isn't it. If you want to build something and stay close to what happens after, it might be.
